statement_record.book: In a locally small C, x and y are representably isomorphic when the represented functors C(-,x) ≅ C(-,y) (and dually C(x,-) ≅ C(y,-)) are naturally isomorphic; such a natural isomorphism is called a representable isomorphism. Isomorphic objects are automatically representably isomorphic.

Program Instance Yoneda_Lemma `(C : Category) `(F : C^op ⟶ Sets) : ∀ A : C, Presheaves [Hom ─,A] F ≅ F A := { to := {| morphism := fun x => transform[x] A id |}; from := {| morphism := fun y : F A => {| transform := fun x : C => {| morphism := fun phi => @fmap (C^op) Sets F A x phi y |} |} |} }.
Lemma preyoneda {C : Category} {c d: C} {P : C^op ⟶ Sets} (τ : [Hom ─ , c] ⟹ P) : forall f : d ~> c, transform τ d f ≈ fmap[P] f (transform τ c id{C}).

statement_record.book: Definition 2.3.3: an ELEMENT of a Set-valued functor F on C is a pair (c, x) with x ∈ Fc; it is UNIVERSAL when the natural transformation Ψ(x) supplied by the Yoneda lemma (C(c,-) ⇒ F covariantly, C(-,c) ⇒ F contravariantly) is a natural ISOMORPHISM. Then c represents F and Ψ(x) is the representation determined by x.
statement_record.intree: { x : F c & IsIsomorphism (from (Yoneda_Lemma C F c) x) }  ≅  Isomorphism [Hom ─,c] F   (an isomorphism of setoids in Sets), where `from (Yoneda_Lemma C F c) x` is exactly Ψ(x) : [Hom ─,c] ⟹ F.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger on the content, intree-narrower on variance: the sigma type IS Riehl's 'element x of Fc whose Yoneda image is an isomorphism', and the library additionally PROVES that universal elements and representations are the same data (Riehl only remarks this). Riehl states the definition in both variances; the in-tree correspondence is proved only contravariantly (F : C^op ⟶ Sets), although Covariant_Yoneda_Lemma (Functor/Hom/Yoneda.v:182) supplies the covariant Ψ and the covariant representation packaging is Functor/Representable.v's Representable class.

statement_record.book: Exercise 2.3.iii: B^A represents the contravariant functor Set(- × A, B) : Set^op → Set; its universal element is the evaluation map ev : B^A × A → B. Define ev and describe the universal property it satisfies, in analogy with the universal bilinear map ⊗ of Example 2.3.8 (every f : X × A → B factors uniquely through ev along a map X → B^A).
statement_record.intree: Class Closed carries exp_iso {x y z} : x × y ~> z ≊ x ~> z^y (Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v:51); eval {x y} : y^x × x ~> y := uncurry id (line 75); ump_exponents (f : x × y ~> z) : eval ∘ first (curry f) ≈ f (line 78); uniqueness from curry_uncurry / uncurry_curry (lines 101/107); naturality in the varying argument from curry_comp_l : curry f ∘ g ≈ curry (f ∘ first g) (line 165). Sets_Closed instantiates all of it with z^y = the setoid of ≈-respecting maps and exp_iso = literal currying.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, and constructively instantiated in the exercise's own category. exp_iso IS the representation Hom(- × y, z) ≅ Hom(-, z^y); eval is the universal element (the image of id under uncurry, i.e. the Yoneda image of the identity); ump_exponents + curry_uncurry are exactly 'every f factors uniquely through ev'; curry_comp_l is the naturality Riehl's 'represents' requires in the varying contravariant argument. The only presentational differences: Sets is setoids rather than bare sets (faithful, per the frozen rule), and naturality appears as a substitution law rather than as a packaged natural transformation.
